functions.name: texp
functions.body: if numberp(x) and x<0 then concat("\\left(",tex1(x),"\\right)") else tex1(x)

functions.name: texsumf
functions.body: block([L:first(args(e))], concat(tex1(first(L)), apply(sconcat, map(lambda([t], concat("+",texp(t))), rest(L)))))

functions.name: texnsum
functions.body: block([L:first(args(e))], concat(tex1(first(L)), apply(sconcat, map(lambda([t], if numberp(t) and t<0 then concat("-",tex1(-t)) else concat("+",tex1(t))), rest(L)))))

functions.name: cft
functions.body: concat(if c<0 then "-" else (if fst then "" else "+"), if abs(c)=1 then "" else tex1(abs(c)), tex1(s))

functions.name: texlin
functions.body: block([L:args(e), out:"", f:true], for k:1 thru length(L) step 2 do (if L[k]#0 then (out:concat(out, cft(L[k],L[k+1],f)), f:false)), if out="" then "0" else out)

questiontext:
The unit vector in the direction of \(\mathbf{a}={{CT:0}}\,\mathbf{i}+{{CT:1}}\,\mathbf{j}+{{CT:2}}\,\mathbf{k}\) is

\( \hat{\mathbf{a}}= \) [[input:ans1]] \(\mathbf{i}\) \(+\) [[input:ans2]] \(\mathbf{j}\) \(+\) [[input:ans3]] \(\mathbf{k}\).
[[validation:ans1]] [[validation:ans2]] [[validation:ans3]]

Enter your answer exactly, using the sqrt function for square roots if necessary, for example inputting \( \sqrt{3} \) as sqrt(3).
generalfeedback:
Outline: The unit vector in the direction of \(\mathbf{a}\) is \(\mathbf{a}\) divided by its magnitude, \(\hat{\mathbf{a}}=\frac{\mathbf{a}}{\mid \mathbf{a} \mid}\). First compute the magnitude, then divide each component by it.
Step 1 — The magnitude
The magnitude of \(\mathbf{a}\), denoted \(\mid \mathbf{a} \mid\), is the square root of the sum of the squares of its components:

\[ \mid \mathbf{a} \mid=\sqrt{ {{CT:3}} }=\sqrt{ {{CT:4}} }=\sqrt{ {{CT:5}} } \]

[[if test="{{CT:13}}"]]Hence

\[ \mid \mathbf{a} \mid={{CT:6}} \]

[[elif test="{{CT:14}}"]]Taking the square factor out of the root:

\[ \mid \mathbf{a} \mid=\sqrt{ {{CT:7}}\cdot {{CT:8}} }={{CT:9}}\sqrt{ {{CT:8}} } \]

[[/if]]
Step 2 — Dividing by the magnitude
Dividing \(\mathbf{a}\) by its magnitude gives a vector of magnitude 1 in the same direction (dividing by a positive number does not change the direction). Each component is divided by \(\mid \mathbf{a} \mid\):

\[ \hat{\mathbf{a}}=\frac{\mathbf{a}}{\mid \mathbf{a} \mid}=\frac{ {{CT:0}} }{\mid \mathbf{a} \mid}\,\mathbf{i}+\frac{ {{CT:1}} }{\mid \mathbf{a} \mid}\,\mathbf{j}+\frac{ {{CT:2}} }{\mid \mathbf{a} \mid}\,\mathbf{k} \]

Substituting the magnitude:[[if test="{{CT:13}}"]]

\[ \hat{\mathbf{a}}=\frac{ {{CT:0}} }{ {{CT:9}} }\,\mathbf{i}+\frac{ {{CT:1}} }{ {{CT:9}} }\,\mathbf{j}+\frac{ {{CT:2}} }{ {{CT:9}} }\,\mathbf{k} \]

[[elif test="{{CT:14}}"]]

\[ \hat{\mathbf{a}}=\frac{ {{CT:0}} }{ {{CT:9}}\sqrt{ {{CT:8}} } }\,\mathbf{i}+\frac{ {{CT:1}} }{ {{CT:9}}\sqrt{ {{CT:8}} } }\,\mathbf{j}+\frac{ {{CT:2}} }{ {{CT:9}}\sqrt{ {{CT:8}} } }\,\mathbf{k} \]

[[else]]

\[ \hat{\mathbf{a}}=\frac{ {{CT:0}} }{\sqrt{ {{CT:8}} } }\,\mathbf{i}+\frac{ {{CT:1}} }{\sqrt{ {{CT:8}} } }\,\mathbf{j}+\frac{ {{CT:2}} }{\sqrt{ {{CT:8}} } }\,\mathbf{k} \]

[[/if]]After simplifying the fractions:

\[ \hat{\mathbf{a}}={{CT:10}}\,\mathbf{i}+{{CT:11}}\,\mathbf{j}+{{CT:12}}\,\mathbf{k}. \]

on_true.feedback: The vector you have input is parallel to the vector \(\textbf{a}\), and it is a unit vector, but it is in the opposite direction to \(\textbf{a}\).

The magnitude of this vector is

\[\sqrt{\left({@ans1@}\right)^2+\left({@ans2@}\right)^2+\left({@ans3@}\right)^2}={@ans_mag@}.\]

You may have divided by the square of a magnitude when you should have divided by a magnitude.

The magnitude of this vector is

\[\sqrt{\left({@ans1@}\right)^2+\left({@ans2@}\right)^2+\left({@ans3@}\right)^2}={@ans_mag@}.\]

It is a unit vector, but it is not in the correct direction.

on_false.feedback:
The magnitude of this vector is

\[\sqrt{\left({@ans1@}\right)^2+\left({@ans2@}\right)^2+\left({@ans3@}\right)^2}={@ans_mag@}\mbox{.}\]

But a unit vector has magnitude 1.
